summary: Don Elkins (1930–1984) was a University of Louisville physics and engineering professor, later an airline captain, who researched UFO contactee messages from 1955 and ran a group channeling experiment from 1962. profile: Don Elkins was born in Louisville, Kentucky, on 27 February 1930, trained as a mechanical engineer and taught physics and engineering at the University of Louisville from 1953 to 1965 before leaving tenure to fly Boeing 727s as an airline captain, which he did until his death ([L/L Research bio](https://www.llresearch.org/about/don-elkins)). At seventeen he had been a flying student of Capt. Thomas Mantell, who died chasing a reported UFO on 7 January 1948; L/L Research dates his UFO research to 1955 and says he conducted about 200 regressive-hypnosis sessions between 1955 and 1960 ([history talk](https://www.llresearch.org/speeches/the-history-of-llresearch)).

In 1961 or 1962 (L/L's pages differ) Elkins received the 'Brown Notebook' of a Detroit contactee group through Hal Price, and in 1962 he began an experiment in which about twelve physics students attempted to reproduce contactee messages in a controlled meditation setting; Carla Rueckert joined as the thirteenth member ([Book I introduction](https://assets.llresearch.org/ra-contact/resources/original_introduction.pdf); [L/L history](https://www.llresearch.org/history)). Elkins and Rueckert formed L/L Research in 1970 and co-wrote *Secrets of the UFO*, first printed in May 1977, in which he argued that over 90 percent of contactee material carried the same message and adopted the word 'density' for levels of reality ([Secrets of the UFO](https://assets.llresearch.org/books/secrets_of_the_ufo.pdf)).

On 15 January 1981, three weeks after Jim McCarty moved to Louisville, a session in which Rueckert and Elkins were teaching a student to channel produced a voice announcing 'I am Ra. I have not spoken through this instrument before' ([Ra session 1](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/ra-contact/1)). Elkins acted as questioner in all 106 sessions, which ran until 15 March 1984 ([session list](https://www.lawofone.info/sessions.php)). He described the method as 'tuned trance telepathy' and his own stance as 'purely scientific', while conceding in print that evidential proof was 'not obtainable' ([Introduction](https://www.lawofone.info/Intro)).

The published material presents Ra as a 'sixth-density social memory complex' from Venus and a member of a 'Confederation of Planets in the Service of the Infinite Creator', and sets out the density octave, 'harvest', 'Wanderers' and the 'Orion group' vocabulary that later ET channels reused ([Ra session 6](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/ra-contact/6); [session 16](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/ra-contact/16)). The sessions also asked whether the 'harvest' would occur in 2011, to which Ra replied 'This is an approximation'; the date passed without the predicted shift, as skeptics note ([lawofone.info Harvest](https://www.lawofone.info/c/Harvest); [RationalWiki](https://rationalwiki.org/wiki/Ra_Material)).

Elkins died on 7 November 1984 'after a year of declining health', according to the L/L epilogue, and the Ra contact ended with him ([epilogue, reproduced](https://www.superphysics.org/research/other/alien/ra/epilogue/)). L/L Research's own bio gives only the year; Find a Grave and IMDb record a self-inflicted gunshot wound ([Find a Grave](https://nl.findagrave.com/memorial/220756481/donald_tully-elkins); [IMDb](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0253859/bio/)). After his death Rueckert and McCarty continued conscious channeling of 'Q'uo', and L/L Research still publishes sessions in 2026 ([L/L channeling archive](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling)).

profile: Carla Lisbeth Rueckert was born on 16 July 1943 in Lake Forest, Illinois, survived kidney failure at thirteen, and joined Don Elkins's meditation group 'in early 1962' as the thirteenth member of his channeling experiment ([Introduction](https://www.lawofone.info/Intro); [L/L bio](https://www.llresearch.org/about/carla-rueckert)). She took a BA in English Literature (1966) and an MA in Library Service (1971) at the University of Louisville, became Elkins's partner in 1968 and left her school-librarian job in January 1970 to work with him full time, the year L/L Research was formed ([L/L history](https://www.llresearch.org/history)).

By her own account she 'did not learn to channel until 1974' ([archive vol. 3](https://assets.llresearch.org/books/ll_research_archive_volume_03.pdf)). Her early conscious contact was 'almost always Hatonn', followed by Latwii, Laitos, Oxal, L/Leema and Yadda, all presented as members of a 'Confederation of Planets in the Service of the Infinite Creator' ([North Atlantic Books blog](https://www.northatlanticbooks.com/blog/wisdom-how-carla-rueckert-found-channeling-and-found-the-truth/)). She co-wrote *Secrets of the UFO* (1977) with Elkins and appeared with him in radio and television interviews from 1976 ([Secrets of the UFO](https://assets.llresearch.org/books/secrets_of_the_ufo.pdf)).

On 15 January 1981, during a session teaching a student to channel, Rueckert entered an unconscious trance and a source identifying itself as Ra spoke through her for the first time; the contact continued for 106 sessions until 15 March 1984, with Elkins as questioner and Jim McCarty as scribe ([Ra session 1](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/ra-contact/1); [session list](https://www.lawofone.info/sessions.php)). L/L Research states that 'Only the 106 sessions of the Ra contact used the trance channeling technique' and that it no longer works with Ra or the trance state ([L/L channeling](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling); [epilogue](https://www.superphysics.org/research/other/alien/ra/epilogue/)). She wrote that she did not know how the trance occurred and called the contact 'a source of some disquiet' ([Introduction](https://www.lawofone.info/Intro)).

After Elkins's death in November 1984 she and McCarty kept the weekly Sunday sessions going; the earliest archived 'Q'uo' session is dated 12 January 1986, and Q'uo is described as a principle combining Hatonn, Latwii and Ra ([1986 archive](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/1986); [2024 circle](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/2024/0509)). She married McCarty on 30 May 1987, published *A Channeling Handbook* (1987), *A Wanderer's Handbook* (2001) and *Living the Law of One 101* (2009), and co-channeled *The Aaron/Q'uo Dialogues* with Barbara Brodsky from 1991 ([L/L bio](https://www.llresearch.org/about/carla-rueckert); [1991 session](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling/1991/0228_02)).

Rueckert described herself as a Christian mystic devoted to Jesus Christ and received weekly communion at home in her final years ([eulogy](https://www.llresearch.org/articles/carlas-eulogy)). Her last channeling session was on 2 April 2011, followed two weeks later by spinal-fusion surgery and repeated infections; she died on 1 April 2015 ([history talk](https://www.llresearch.org/speeches/the-history-of-llresearch); [L/L bio](https://www.llresearch.org/about/carla-rueckert)). Skeptics note that the Ra material's c. 2011 'harvest' approximation passed without observable change ([RationalWiki](https://rationalwiki.org/wiki/Ra_Material)); L/L Research continues the conscious-channeling circle she helped train, with sessions dated 2026 ([L/L channeling](https://www.llresearch.org/channeling)).

summary: George Van Tassel (1910–1978) was a Giant Rock, California contactee who claimed telepathic contact with 'Ashtar', a space-fleet commander, from 18 July 1952, and hosted the Giant Rock Spacecraft Conventions from 1953. Claimed a physical encounter on 1953-08-24 with 'Solgonda' of Venus, who gave a formula for a rejuvenation machine, the Integratron, begun in 1954 and unfinished at his death.
Presented extraterrestrials as having influenced humanity and religious texts; the earliest messages reference a 'Council of the Seven Lights'.
His Ministry later disowned the breakaway 'Ashtar Command' messages as 'a clone of the original Ashtar'.

profile: George W. Van Tassel was born in Jefferson, Ohio, in 1910 (10 or 12 March; sources differ) and in 1947 leased Giant Rock, a seven-storey boulder in the Mojave Desert near Landers, California, where he ran an airstrip and café ([Wikipedia: Giant Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Rock); [WRSP profile](https://wrldrels.org/2016/12/05/ashtar-command/)). In 1948 he founded a weekly meditation group, the Brotherhood of the Cosmic Christ, and the World Religions and Spirituality Project dates his first telepathic 'spaceship' messages to 6 January 1952 ([WRSP](https://wrldrels.org/2016/12/05/ashtar-command/)).

On 18 July 1952 he reported the first message from 'Ashtar', who introduced himself as 'commandant quadra sector, patrol station Schare' and warned that hydrogen-bomb research threatened life on Earth ([Encyclopedia.com](https://encyclopedia.com/science/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/ashtar); [CDAMM](https://www.cdamm.org/articles/extraterrestrial)). The first US H-bomb test on 1 November 1952 passed without the predicted catastrophe; later messages claimed Ashtar's forces had helped the planet survive ([WRSP](https://wrldrels.org/2016/12/05/ashtar-command/)). His book *I Rode a Flying Saucer* appeared the same year ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Van_Tassel)).

From spring 1953 Van Tassel hosted the annual Giant Rock Interplanetary Spacecraft Convention, which Wikipedia says ran to 1971 with a 1959 peak of about 10,000 attendees, while WRSP gives 1977 and 'up to 11,000'; *Life* magazine covered it on 27 May 1957 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Van_Tassel); [WRSP](https://wrldrels.org/2016/12/05/ashtar-command/)). He also published the newsletter *Proceedings of the College of Universal Wisdom* from 1953 and founded the Ministry of Universal Wisdom (1952 or 1953).

Van Tassel said that on 24 August 1953 he was physically visited by 'Solgonda' of Venus and other beings from a scout ship, who gave him the formula for a time and rejuvenation machine; he began building the Integratron in 1954 and it was still unfinished, described as '95% complete', when he died ([Wikipedia: Ashtar Sheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashtar_Sheran); [WRSP](https://wrldrels.org/2016/12/05/ashtar-command/)). Within months of the first Ashtar message, Robert Short broke away after Van Tassel rejected his Ashtar messages and founded the 'Ashtar Command'; Van Tassel's Ministry later called such messages 'a clone of the original Ashtar' ([Kook Science](https://hatch.kookscience.com/wiki/Ashtar)).

Scholars treat Van Tassel as a founding figure of the contactee movement: Brenda Denzler calls him 'probably the most important person' in it, Christopher Helland argues that Ashtar belief rests on 'faith in an extraterrestrial celebrity', and Andreas Grünschloss likens much Ashtar channeling to cargo cults ([Wikipedia: Ashtar Sheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashtar_Sheran)). Van Tassel died of a heart attack in a Santa Ana hotel room on 9 February 1978, weeks before the Integratron's planned opening ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Van_Tassel)). After his death Tuella became Ashtar's main spokesperson, and the name has since been claimed by channels from Yvonne Cole (1986) to Athina Król (2026) ([Encyclopedia.com](https://encyclopedia.com/science/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/ashtar)).
